review_notes: Diff: platform/src/lib/retrieval/{envelope.ts, registry/layers/reading_checklist.ts, registry/layers/register_d9_judgment.ts, registry/layers/register_d8_assess_domain.ts, registry/layers/__tests__/reading_checklist.fetch_gochara_sweep_past_peak.test.ts}. fetchGocharaSweep ranked kala_gochara_windows by interval-overlap + ABS(signed_intensity) but never compared peak_date against as_of_date, so an already-peaked window (incl. the repro's top-ranked window, peaked >1yr prior) was served identically to a genuinely future one with no distinguishing field. Fix adds GocharaSweepWindow.is_past_peak (null when peak_date is null, honest can't-tell), GocharaSweepResult.past_peak_window_count (aggregate over full overlap-matched set, not just top-5 slice), a new info-severity judgment_flags entry (gochara_top_window_already_peaked) in register_d9_judgment.ts keyed on windows[0], and the corresponding passthrough in register_d8_assess_domain.ts (covers all 4 assess_* tools via shared dispatcher) plus the JUDGMENT_FLAG_CODES vocabulary registration in envelope.ts (required for the TS union type judgmentFlag() checks against). Design choice is flag-in-place not filter-out, correctly justified against B.10/N.6 (never silently drop served data) and matches the F-34/CL-13 exemplar pattern already established for this class of finding. Corpus artifacts (builder/reviewer/ratifier/verifier_v, all ingested results/ingested/F-134.*.json) independently reached COMPLETE/PASS with detailed line-level spot-checks; this pass re-verified independently rather than trusting that record: (1) confirmed live diff matches the reviser's own spec verbatim; (2) confirmed judgmentFlag(code, detail, severity) 3-arg signature against envelope.ts; (3) the one real correctness risk I checked for — whether Postgres DATE columns arrive as JS Date objects (which would make the peakDate < start string comparison silently always-false via NaN coercion) rather than strings — is closed: platform/src/lib/db/client.ts explicitly registers types.setTypeParser(types.builtins.DATE, (v) => v), so peak_date/window_start/window_end all arrive as raw 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings, matching the existing string-comparison pattern already used elsewhere in the same function. No bugs found. Small work, self-contained, additive-only (rollback is a clean single-commit revert per the spec's own §7).
